title: Jaka Food Processing v. Pacot
summary: The Supreme Court clarified the requirements for valid retrenchment under Article 283 of the Labor Code, ruling that the employer must prove actual or imminent substantial losses and that retrenchment is reasonably necessary to avert such losses.
doctrine: For a valid retrenchment, the employer must prove: (1) substantial and actual or imminent losses; (2) that retrenchment is reasonably necessary and likely to prevent the expected losses; (3) good faith; and (4) fair and reasonable criteria in selecting employees to be retrenched. The burden of proof rests on the employer.
fullText:
GARCIA, J.:

This case involves the legality of the retrenchment of several employees by the petitioner company on the ground of serious business losses.

Article 283 of the Labor Code authorizes the employer to terminate the employment of any employee due to retrenchment to prevent losses. However, the employer must prove that the losses are substantial, serious, actual and real, or if only expected, are reasonably imminent.

The employer must also show that it exercised good faith in implementing the retrenchment and that it used fair and reasonable criteria in ascertaining who would be dismissed and who would be retained. Mere allegations of projected losses without competent evidence are not sufficient.
